note: Terminal-side adversarial rows for the snapshot witness contract. Every value is invented: there is no live account, holding, owner id or database behind any of it. The shared cross-language cases live in projection_cases.json; these are the cases that go BEYOND them — the reader divergences the producer's own Python mirror gets wrong, and the cases that must still be ACCEPTED because they are harmless.

cases.name: unicode_arabic_digit_shares
cases.why: CPython's float() accepts Unicode decimal digits and so does the producer's mirror (its regex uses \d, which is Unicode-aware in Python); JavaScript's Number() does not. The Terminal reads no shares, the composer would read 12 — the two readers disagree, so the row is refused.

cases.name: unicode_fullwidth_digit_shares
cases.why: The same divergence with fullwidth digits: Python reads 12, the Terminal reads nothing.

cases.name: unicode_decimal_point_shares
cases.why: A Unicode full stop with ASCII digits: Python reads 1.5, the Terminal reads nothing.

cases.name: upper_divergent_ticker
cases.why: Python's str.upper() and JavaScript's toUpperCase() differ on U+019B (among 55 code points), so the ticker has no single reading. Refused rather than resolved in either language's favour.

cases.name: strip_divergent_ticker
cases.why: Python's str.strip() removes U+0085 and JavaScript's trim() does not, so the two readers see different tickers.

cases.name: bom_prefixed_ticker
cases.why: JavaScript's trim() removes U+FEFF and Python's strip() does not — the mirrored case of the one above.

cases.name: hex_numeric_string_shares
cases.why: JavaScript's Number() reads 0x10 as 16; Python's float() rejects it. The readers disagree.

cases.name: underscore_numeric_string_shares
cases.why: Python's float() reads PEP 515 underscores (1_0 is 10); JavaScript's Number() rejects it.

cases.name: boolean_shares
cases.why: Python's float(True) is 1.0; JavaScript refuses a boolean outright.

cases.name: non_finite_exponent_shares
cases.why: 1e400 overflows to infinity in both readers; a non-finite cost is never a cost.

cases.name: unicode_ticker_ordinary
cases.why: A non-ASCII ticker whose characters upper-case identically in both languages is NOT ambiguous — the readers agree and the row is accepted.

cases.name: unicode_notes_kept
cases.why: Notes never reach the composer. Unicode, emoji and newlines in a note are carried verbatim and change only the canonical book key.

cases.name: currency_receipt_verbatim
cases.why: The currency receipt is preserved verbatim and the Terminal derives the currency from the same bytes through its own unchanged projection.

cases.name: status_closed_padded
cases.why: ' closed ' is closed: the canonical status rule trims and lowercases before it compares.

cases.name: status_null_is_open
cases.why: A missing status reads OPEN — the canonical rule treats anything that is not exactly 'closed' as open.

cases.name: closed_row_is_not_gated
cases.why: A closed row never reaches the composer, so the two readers cannot disagree about the BRIEF about it. It is carried verbatim and enters the book key through the unchanged rowToPosition — gating it would refuse a witness the producer is entitled to emit.
